name: A forbidden marriage
about: The children of two houses that hate each other fall in love; a parent forbids it, and they obey, elope or are hunted, while the houses' strength decides who keeps them.
title: The Forbidden Match of {a.houseName} and {b.houseName}
fade: {a} and {b} stop writing. Whatever it was, {thread} is a song now, sung wrong.

beats.speaker: a
text: At the harvest fair in {elder.seat}, {a} of {a.house} and {b} of {b.house} dance three dances together, and are seen.
{a} and {b} meet at a hawking party neither house should have attended, and ride back far behind the others.

memory.a: I danced with {b} of {b.house}. I think of nothing else.
memory.b: I met {a} of {a.house}, whose house my {b.father} hates. I do not care.

beats.speaker: b
beats.text: Letters pass between {a} and {b}, hidden in loaves and saddlebags. A maid of {elder.house} reads one, and tells.

memory.elder: My {a.son} {a} has been writing to {b}, the {b.son} of {rival}.

beats.speaker: elder
beats.text: {a} kneels before {elder} and asks leave to wed {b} of {rival.house}. {elder} says {elder.he} will think on it, and sends a rider to {rival}.

beats.speaker: elder
beats.text: Bells ring in {elder.seat}: {a} weds {b}, and {elder.house} and {rival.house} drink from one cup. Old grudges are buried, for now.

memory.elder: I let my {a.son} wed into {rival.house}. Let it end the old quarrel.
memory.rival: My {b.son} {b} wed {a} of {elder.house}. We are kin now, {elder} and I.

beats.speaker: elder
beats.text: {elder} forbids it: no child of {elder.house} will wed into {rival.house}. {a} is locked in a tower room at {elder.seat}.

memory.a: {elder} forbade me {b} and locked me in a tower like a thief.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: {a} bows to {elder}'s will. {b} is promised elsewhere within the year, and {a} does not go to the feast.

memory.a: I gave up {b} because {elder} commanded it. I will not forgive it.

a.text: make {elder} answer for what was taken from me

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: {a} slips out of {elder.seat} by the sally port and rides for {b}. They are wed by a hedge priest at dawn, with a ploughman for a witness.

memory.a: I wed {b} by a hedge priest at dawn. Let them come.
memory.b: {a} came to me through the night. We are wed.
memory.elder: My {a.son} ran off to wed into {rival.house}. A theft, and {rival} is the thief.
memory.rival: My {b.son} wed {a} of {elder.house} without my leave.

beats.speaker: elder
beats.text: {elder} calls the match a theft and rides on {rival.seat} with steel to take {a} back.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: {elder}'s riders drag {a} back to {elder.seat}. The priests unmake the marriage; {b} is left bleeding at the roadside.

memory.a: My {elder.father}'s men dragged me home and the priests unmade my marriage to {b}.
memory.b: {elder}'s riders took {a} from me on the road and left me in the ditch.

die.how: I died on the road trying to keep {a}.

beats.speaker: b
beats.text: {elder}'s host turns for home. {a} and {b} keep their hearth under {rival.house}'s banners, and a child is born before the snows.

memory.a: My {elder.father} could not take me back. My home is with {b} now.

beats.speaker: elder
beats.text: {elder} rages for a week, then sends a cask of wine after the couple. A match made is a match made.
Death parts {a} and {b} before the houses can. In {elder.seat} and {rival.seat} alike the bells are rung, and each house blames the other.
